What is Gamma?

AI presentation and document tool that generates decks, documents and web pages from a prompt or pasted content, using a flexible card-based format rather than fixed slide dimensions - so output works equally as a deck, a scrolling page or a site.

Best for

Getting from raw content to a presentable, on-brand deck fastest.

Main features

  • Generate a full deck from a prompt, outline, pasted text or uploaded document
  • card-based responsive format that adapts to any screen
  • AI editing of individual cards
  • built-in image generation and stock search
  • themes and brand kit with custom fonts and colours
  • publish as a website with a custom domain
  • analytics on who viewed what
  • embed video, charts, Figma, Loom and more
  • PowerPoint and PDF export
  • collaboration and commenting.

Practical use cases

  • Turning a long document into a pitch deck in minutes
  • producing a client proposal that works as both a deck and a shareable link
  • creating course material
  • building a quick landing page
  • internal updates with view analytics.

Who is it for?

  • Startups, consultants, marketers, educators, sales teams and anyone who makes decks regularly but is not a designer.

Pricing, free access & limits

Freemium credit-based subscription

Plans described in the source

Free $0 with 400 one-time AI credits on signup, unlimited basic decks, but a 'Made with Gamma' badge on shared content. Plus around $10/mo ($8 annually) with 400 credits/month, badge removal and unlimited AI edits. Pro around $20/mo ($15 annually) with unlimited AI credits, advanced image models, custom fonts, detailed analytics and priority support. Business and Enterprise tiers with SSO, admin controls and shared brand kits. Annual billing roughly 20-25% cheaper.

Free plan

Yes - free tier with 400 one-time credits and unlimited manual deck creation, but shared output carries a Gamma badge.

Free trial

The free credits serve as the trial; Pro trials occasionally offered.

Usage limits to consider

Credit-metered on Free and Plus - generating a deck consumes credits, as does AI image generation and card-level AI editing. Pro removes credit limits. The Gamma badge appears on Free tier output.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Fastest path from content to a decent-looking deck of anything in this group
  • the card format producing deck, doc and web page from one artefact is genuinely clever and more useful than it first sounds
  • view analytics on shared links are valuable for sales
  • output looks good without design skill.

Limitations to consider

  • The card format is not real PowerPoint - export to PPTX loses fidelity and breaks complex layouts, which is a problem if your organisation requires PPTX deliverables
  • less precise layout control than PowerPoint or Figma
  • credit consumption on Plus is easy to exhaust
  • RTL and Arabic typography need testing
  • designs, while good, are recognisably Gamma.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web, iOS, Android

Languages

  • Generates in many languages including Arabic and French; RTL support has improved but should be tested

API access

Yes - Gamma API in beta/early access for programmatic generation

Integrations and exports

  • PowerPoint and PDF export, Google Drive import, Figma embed, Loom, YouTube, Airtable, custom domains for published sites

Evaluation notes

If your deliverable must be an editable PowerPoint file, test the export on a real deck before committing - this is Gamma's weakest point. If the deliverable is a shared link, Gamma is the strongest tool here.
